title: Why governments intervene

match.reason: The bank point covers government-owned enterprises in Year 11 Business Studies, not why governments intervene in the economy, so it teaches a different idea at a different depth.

draft.title: Why governments intervene
card: Governments step into the economy because markets left alone do not always give fair or good results. Stepping in is called intervention.
Some goods, such as street lighting and national defence, are hard to charge for because everyone can use them. Private firms rarely supply them, so governments often do.
Governments protect consumers from unsafe products and unfair business practices. They also protect the environment from harm that firms may ignore.
Governments may reduce inequality by helping people on low incomes. They may also try to smooth out booms and slumps, so the economy does not swing too far up or down.
draft.remember: Governments step in to provide public goods, protect people and the environment, reduce inequality and smooth booms and slumps.

a.q: Why does the government, rather than private firms, usually provide street lighting?
opts: Everyone can use it, so firms struggle to charge for it
It is too cheap for any firm to make a profit from
It only helps people with low incomes in a town
It is a consumer product that needs safety checks
a.why: Street lighting is a public good. Everyone can use it, so a firm cannot easily charge people, and few firms would supply it. It is not about low incomes or product safety.
a.clue: Think about whether a firm could stop people using the light.

b.q: A chemical factory near a town in the Hunter Valley is dumping waste into a river. The NSW Government steps in and fines the factory. Which reason for intervention does this show?
opts: Protecting the environment from harm that firms may ignore
Providing a public good that firms will not supply
Smoothing out a slump in the economy
Reducing inequality between high and low incomes
b.why: The fine aims to stop harm to the river, so it protects the environment. It is not a public good, because the factory is not supplying something everyone uses, and it does not target a slump or income gaps.
b.clue: What is being harmed by the factory?

a.best: Everyone can use it, so firms struggle to charge for it

b.best: Protecting the environment from harm that firms may ignore
